REGULAR MEETING AGENDA - REVISED
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS

COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA WILL PARTICIPATE VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM HYATT HOUSE CHICAGO, 2ND FLOOR BREAKFAST AREA,
1835 W. HARRISON STREET,CHICAGO, IL 60612, AND THIS AGENDA WILL BE POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE
THURSDAY - AUGUST 22, 2024 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, AUGUST 22, 2024,
7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER YOKOYAMA PARTICIPATED VIA
TELECONFERENCE FROM HYATT HOUSE CHICAGO, 2ND FLOOR BREAKFAST AREA,
1835 W. HARRISON STREET, CHICAGO, IL 60612, AND THE AGENDA FOR THIS MEETING
WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT
CODE.

 4.  Roll Call

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson

  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo

  comments submitted for meeting items by the deadline listed on the agenda and for
  inclusion in the official record. Requests for copies of the written comments submitted

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  David Pylman stated the jurisdiction of the legislative body should be considered as part

  amendment items listed on the Consent Calendar.

  Susanne Fermin, Public Relations Manager, World Mission Society Church of God,
  announced their services and programs, requesting the City’s endorsement of their

  the Way of Hope, Asez Wao, World Mission Society Church of God Young Adult Worker
  Volunteer Group.” (Documents submitted to the City Council at a public meeting are
  considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text, redacted written
  correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City
  Clerk/Treasurer).

  Peter Park expressed concern regarding trash dumping at an ABC Unified School District
  lot, near the Cerritos Villas, by one (1) or more entities that have contracted work with
  the City.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to review the contract with Onyx Paving
  Company, Inc. for arterial street rehabilitation, for omissions and, if necessary,
  compose a boilerplate contract clause to mitigate future construction staging issues,
  provide updates to residents, and schedule an agenda report on a future meeting
  agenda concerning the issue and if needed, an acceptable clause to include on future,
  similar contracts.

  Jason Chou expressed concern regarding trash dumping by regarding trash dumping at
  an ABC Unified School District lot, near the Cerritos Villas, by one (1) or more entities
  that have contracted work with the City.

  Tony Park expressed concern regarding trash dumping at an ABC Unified School District
  lot, near the Cerritos Villas, by one (1) or more entities that have contracted work with
  the City.

  Sam Desai expressed concern regarding contractors using loopholes for their own
  purposes. He also expressed concern with public meeting protocol and the ad hoc
  working group process.

  Marin Bravu expressed concern regarding threats of bomb and gun violence at Whitney
  High School and other ABC Unified School District schools.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Written comments, if submitted by the deadline listed on the agenda, are considered

7B.4. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Johnson, to authorize
  administrative-initiated Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with
  Joint Budget Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan
  and Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project:  Multiple
  Amount:  $945,000 (transfer from FY 2023-24)
  Justification: A carryover of unexpended funds from the prior fiscal year is
  requested for capital equipment that was ordered but not yet received at fiscal
  year-end. The delay in delivery has been caused by ongoing nationwide supply
  chain issues. This carryover will ensure that the necessary funds remain
  available to complete the purchases when the equipment arrives. Please refer to
  Exhibit 1 of the agenda report associated with this Agenda Item, for a detailed list of
  the equipment.

  2. Account/Project:  110-211-51010 (Regular Earnings)
  110-211-52400 (Employee Benefits)
  Amount:  $134,822 (Transfer)
  $527 (New Allocation)
  Justification: The Department of Community Development is requesting a
  budget amendment to reclassify the Division Secretary position (Grade 32) in the
  Current Planning Division to a Department Secretary position (Grade 35) in the
  Office of the Director. This reclassification is necessary due to existing
  administrative vacancies within the department and the ongoing need to support
  Planning Commission operations. The change will enhance administrative
  efficiencies, ensure continued support for the Planning Commission, and maintain
  the effective delivery of Community Development services to the public

  ;(COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (3 – 0 – 2 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Vo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Yokoyama, Solanki
  ABSTAIN:  None

  4 well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the
  continued existence of a local emergency as specified; and
